claim: Reviewing a weaker model's code draft with a stronger frontier model raises pass rate from 71.6% to 89.7% on LiveCodeBench hard/medium tasks.
scope_conditions: 116 hard/medium LiveCodeBench tasks, single-file Python competitive programming problems, static review (no test execution), Claude Opus 4.7 and Codex GPT-5.5 only
quoted_support: Claude Opus 4.7 review raises Codex GPT-5.5 drafts from 71.6% to 89.7% (p_BH=.001)

claim: Having a weaker model review a stronger model's code draft reduces pass rate from 91.4% to 82.8%, i.e. adversarial review can actively harm correctness.
stance_target: adversarial cross-model review reliably improves code correctness
scope_conditions: Same LiveCodeBench setup; Codex GPT-5.5 reviewing Claude Opus 4.7 drafts
quoted_support: Codex GPT-5.5 reviewing Claude Opus 4.7 drafts drops the pass rate from 91.4% to 82.8% (p_BH=.046)

claim: Same-model self-review (a model reviewing its own code draft) produces no significant accuracy change when the writer model is already strong, consistent with Olausson et al.'s finding that self-repair gains depend on whether the repairer is meaningfully stronger than the drafter.
stance_target: second-pass review value depends on relative model capability, not model distinctness alone
quoted_support: Claude Opus 4.7 reviewing itself stays at 91.4%... AA matches A's pass rate while adding 72% to cost and 58% to latency

claim: A harmful reviewer tends to discard the writer's working data structure and rewrite from scratch, while a helpful reviewer tends to preserve the writer's interface and patch a single local invariant.
stance_target: mechanism of reviewer-induced regressions in adversarial code review
scope_conditions: Qualitative case analysis of AO (harmful) vs OA/OO (helpful) conditions; interpretive, not a coded taxonomy
quoted_support: Codex GPT-5.5 as reviewer, when uncertain, tends to discard the writer's data structure and start over... Claude Opus 4.7 as reviewer tends to keep the writer's interface and repair one local invariant

claim: Adding a review pass approximately doubles per-task cost ($0.19-0.23 solo vs $0.31-0.44 reviewed) and adds 30-75 seconds of latency, and is only cost-effective when the writer model is the weaker of the pair.
stance_target: cost/latency trade-off of adding adversarial review layer
scope_conditions: 116 LiveCodeBench tasks, vendor-hosted API pricing at time of study
quoted_support: OA adds 21 net passes at an extra $0.25 per task across 116 tasks, or roughly $1.40 per net fix; OO adds 15 net passes at an extra $0.12 per task, or roughly $0.95 per net fix

claim: The study explicitly does not generalize beyond single-file competitive-programming problems to repository-scale bug fixing, multi-file review, build integration, or security/maintainability concerns.
stance_target: scope limits of evidence for Pillar-1 adversarial review mechanism
quoted_support: The setting isolates algorithmic reasoning under contamination-aware evaluation using LiveCodeBench but does not generalize to repository-scale bug fixing, build systems, or multi-file review.
